findings.title: Overly broad delete condition removes all reminders with retryCount > 1 regardless of method
findings.body: The deleteMany OR clause `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` is not scoped to `method: SMS` like the first clause. Since retryCount is a shared field on WorkflowReminder (also potentially used by EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders in the future, or any reminder with a non-SMS method that incidentally has retryCount > 1), this condition could delete non-SMS workflow reminders too. Given this is the SMS-specific scheduling cron, it should scope by method: SMS as well, otherwise it silently deletes unrelated reminders that happen to exceed the threshold.

findings.title: Reminder deleted before scheduledSMS actually succeeds confirmed, and retryCount increments may still allow unlimited retries within a single run due to delete running once at top
findings.body: The deleteMany for retryCount > 1 only runs once at the start of the handler. If a reminder fails scheduling in this same cron run (incrementing retryCount from 1 to 2), it will not be deleted until the next cron invocation, meaning it stays in an invalid state for up to the next run's cadence. This is a minor behavioral inefficiency rather than a hard bug, but combined with the lack of method scoping it increases risk of unexpected reminder loss or persistence.
